summary: Kickoff between Redwood AE/SE and Orchid procurement/legal to align on MSA/DPA redlines, committed usage pricing, SLA targets, and security controls. Key asks: dedicated capacity for PHI-adjacent workflows, KMS integration, SSO with SAML, SOC 2 evidence, and clear overage billing paths. Agreed next steps: Redwood to send redlines and pricing worksheet; SE to provide performance docs for Dedicated and on-prem options; Customer to confirm committed token volumes and legal requirements.
transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hi everyone, thanks for taking the time. We'll do a short agenda run, then Tom will go through the capacity and performance bits, and then we'll land on contract asks. Jill, thanks for organizing this with procurement.
[00:12] Jill (Orchid, Procurement): Thanks Maya. Yep, we've got legal and security on. We want to walk away with a clear path for MSA/DPA, pricing for committed usage and clarity on SLA and support.
[00:23] Tom (Redwood SE): Hey all. Quick note — I'll try to keep the deep perf numbers high level, but happy to deep dive afterwards. We ran the Dedicated cluster tests on 8xA100 equivalent and on the Quantized Llama-ish model family, which showed predictable p99 latencies when token lengths are under 1k.
[00:40] Rajesh (Head of Cloud): Quick clarifying Q — when you say Dedicated is predictable, do you mean reserved VMs in our VPC or your Dedicated managed pool? We need to understand network egress, private peering, and egress billing.
[00:52] Tom: Good question. Two flavors: Redwood Dedicated (we allocate a physical pool in our data plane for your tenancy, optional VPC peering) vs Redwood Private (we can ship a control plane but you run inference in your VPC/on-prem). The Dedicated offering can be VPC peered so traffic stays within your networking and egress billing is managed per our contract. Note: in a true on-prem Private deployment, you control all egress.
[01:15] Morgan (Legal): On the DPA side we have a short list: data residency for PHI-adjacent logs, KMS/HSM key custody, and an audit trail with immutable logs for 7 years. Is that supported out of the box?
[01:28] Tom: KMS integration is supported — we integrate with customer KMS for model ingest and keys at rest. HSM-backed KMS is possible via our KMS connectors. Audit logs exist in the Console, and we can extend retention as an add-on. I will caveat that the default retention is 90 days in hosted consoles.
[01:46] Samir (Security): That default retention is a problem for us. We need at least three years on audit logs and tamper-evidence. Also, can you sign a clause for data subject access requests that routes through our SOC?
[01:58] Maya: We have enterprise add-ons for extended retention and tamper-evidence. For DSAR we typically map request flows in the DPA so we can do that. We'll note Morgan and Samir's ask in the redlines.
[02:08] Jill: Another legal ask — indemnity carve-outs around model hallucinations that lead to patient harm. We understand that Redwood can't promise content accuracy, but we need clear limits and incident response commitments.
[02:21] Maya: Understood. We usually include a standard Warranties and Liability section, and we can add an incident response SLA and an obligation to cooperate on investigations. We should log that for legal redlines.
[02:32] Ivy (Finance): Pricing — we need committed discounts vs pay-as-you-go. What's the typical commitment tiers and overage rates?
[02:40] Maya: Typical is a 12-month committed tokens model with tiers — e.g., 0–1B tokens, 1B–5B, 5B+. Discounts increase with commitment. Overage billing is typically at a blended rate slightly above the committed unit price; we can provide an exact worksheet.
[02:55] Rajesh: For our forecasting we need committed units per month and peaking profile. If we underutilize, is there a carryover or true-up?
[03:04] Maya: We offer two constructs: a smoothing true-up where unused committed tokens can be carried forward for a short window, or a firm reservation with lower unit cost but no carryover. We'll include both options in the pricing worksheet.
[03:16] Tom: Also for cost control we have config knobs — batching, KV cache, sequence-length caps — that materially affect unit cost. For example, enabling prefix KV cache reduced token cost by ~18% in our internal bench on stateful chat patterns.
[03:30] Rajesh: What's the latency impact of batching? Our clinical UI is latency-sensitive.
[03:35] Tom: You can target latency SLOs by configuring max batch latency, and Redwood's smart batcher will prioritize low-latency queues. With our Dedicated SLOs we can guarantee p95 ≤ 220ms for <512 token responses in typical setups; p99 depends more on sequence length and KV hits. We'll include the SLI/SLO language for contract.
[03:53] Morgan: On the MSA redlines: we flagged export control and crypto clauses. We need clarity on who is the data processor vs controller for different flows — e.g., telemetry for model improvements.
[04:05] Maya: We can set telemetry to off for your tenant, or configure it so data used for model improvements is anonymized and requires explicit opt-in. We'll mark that as an available setting in the DPA.
[04:16] [crosstalk] Jill: And HIPAA— are you willing to sign a Business Associate Agreement?
[04:21] Maya: We have customers under HIPAA; we can sign a BAA but that does come with additional controls. Tom, can you speak to redwood's approach to PHI?
[04:29] Tom: Yes. For PHI workflows we recommend either Dedicated with VPC peering or Private. The key is to keep token payloads inside the private network and to enable KMS where only the customer's KMS holds the encryption keys for stored artifacts. Also we offer logging to a customer-managed S3 for audit retention.
[04:46] Samir: We will need to run a security questionnaire and have an onsite (or virtual) security review. Do you have a standard questionnaire or attestation pack?
[04:54] Maya: We maintain an Infosec pack: SOC 2 report, pen test summary, architecture diagrams, and a security questionnaire template. I will share the folder link after the call.
[05:03] Tom: To call out a small nuance — when we talk about KV cache and prefix caching, the cache is encrypted at rest and scoped per-tenant. However, for token-level dedup caching there are operational considerations if you want zero-sharing between tenants on the same physical host; Dedicated gives that guarantee.
[05:21] Jill: Can you summarize the difference again between Hosted with VPC peering and Dedicated? Legal just wants to understand risk surface in the MSA.
[05:30] Maya: Sure. Hosted with VPC peering — we still operate the inference plane, but network peering reduces public internet egress. It's still in our multi-tenant control plane but with tenant isolation at app-level. Dedicated is a reserved pool for your account and we can enforce physical separation of GPUs and host OS as an option. Private means you run the inference plane in your environment and we provide a control plane or software.
[05:50] Morgan: For indemnity and liability, our counsel asked about caps tied to fees and carve-outs for willful misconduct. Is your standard cap 1x ARR?
[05:59] Maya: Standard is 1x fees in the past 12 months, but enterprise customers sometimes negotiate higher caps or carve-outs for certain liabilities. We'll note Morgan's ask.
[06:08] Ivy: For accounting, we need to know whether commitment counts as OPEX vs CAPEX for our financials. Do you provide invoicing monthly? Quarterly? Annual?
[06:16] Maya: We typically invoice monthly for usage and can do monthly or quarterly invoices for committed contracts. We can accommodate preferred billing cadence; we'll reflect options in the pricing worksheet.
[06:26] Tom: One more technical item — support tiers. We offer Standard (business hours email), Premium (24/7 on-call with guaranteed response times), and Enterprise (dedicated CSM + priority escalation). SLAs for platform availability are included in Dedicated agreements; the Hosted default is best-effort unless you buy an SLA addon.
[06:46] Rajesh: For PII and PHI we need 24/7 support with a 1-hour response for Sev1 incidents. Is that part of Enterprise?
[06:54] Maya: Yes, that's Enterprise. We'll include a proposed Sev matrix in the SLA section and map target response/resolution times.
[07:02] Jill: About termination — if we decide to stop the contract mid-year, what's the run-out and data return policy? We want guaranteed deletion and proof-of-deletion.
[07:12] Maya: Our standard is a 90-day run-out for data handoff; we can extend to an agreed period and provide signed proof-of-deletion and a downloadable archive. I'll capture that.
[07:20] Morgan: Also, can you commit to scope-limited subcontractors? We need to list any third-party subprocessors and have a notification period for new ones.
[07:29] Maya: We maintain a subprocessors list and provide 30 days' notice for changes; we can also include subprocessors in the DPA appendices.
[07:39] Tom: I'll flag the required appendix template for subprocessors and the cryptographic key custody language.
[07:46] [08:00] Maya: Switching to pricing specifics — for a 12-month firm commit of 3B tokens/month, here's an example: base unit price X with a 22% discount versus PAYGO, overage billed at 1.25x unit price. We can also offer a smoothing true-up where unused tokens can be carried forward up to three months.
[08:17] Ivy: If we go for the smoothing option, and we underutilize by 30% for two months, does that affect our quarter-end all-in cost modeling? We need predictability.
[08:26] Maya: Smoothing helps predictability; however, finance typically models committed spend as the minimum. We'll put both firm reservation and smoothing cashflows in the worksheet.
[08:36] Rajesh: A technical follow-up — for VPC peering, do you support AWS PrivateLink or just standard VPC peering?
[08:42] Tom: We support VPC peering and PrivateLink in most regions; for sensitive deployments we recommend PrivateLink as it reduces cross-subnet exposure. We'll note region constraints in the runbook.
[08:54] Morgan: Regarding the DPA, we also require breach notification within 48 hours on incidents affecting PHI. Is that acceptable?
[09:01] Maya: We commit to 72-hour notification in standard DPAs, but for enterprise we can negotiate 48 hours with the right controls. We'll surface that as a redline.
[09:10] Samir: On pen tests, do you provide test windows and coordinate with your infra team? We need to run auth-proxied tests against the console and private endpoints.
[09:20] Tom: Yes, we coordinate pen-test windows; our infra team provides guidance. For Private deployments you can run tests directly. For hosted instances we require an approved scope and timeslot.
[09:29] Jill: Can we get the MSA track with inline comments? Our counsel prefers markups rather than a list of asks.
[09:36] Maya: Absolutely — we'll send a redline of the MSA + DPA and also a tracked changes version for ease.
[09:42] [crosstalk] Ivy: On the point of tax and geo billing, are EU customers billed VAT-inclusive? We have entities in both US and EU.
[09:50] Maya: We handle region-based billing and can invoice either entity depending on the contract. We support VAT handling; we'll align with your finance contact.
[09:58] Rajesh: Any blockers for storing tokens or models in EU-only regions for GDPR?
[10:03] Tom: No blocker — we can pin inference and log storage to EU-West region in both Dedicated and Private. For Hosted, we have region footprint and can allocate capacity in EU region under your tenancy.
[10:13] Morgan: Sequence control — we need a provision that restricts Redwood from training models on customer-provided prompts unless explicitly authorized.
[10:18] Maya: That's standard. We'll add an explicit clause that customer data won't be used for model training or improvement unless opted in.
[10:26] Tom: Quick perf nuance — when you enable quantized weights some long-tail token patterns can increase inference jitter; we usually recommend a small canary before broad rollout.
[10:35] Rajesh: Sounds fair. We'll plan a canary pilot.
[10:38] Jill: For signoff path — procurement wants to know the timeline for approvals. We are aiming to have procurement sign by end of March, assuming no major redlines. Is that reasonable?
[10:47] Maya: That's reasonable. If we turn around redlines this week and have parallel legal reviews, late March is feasible.
[10:53] Ivy: Finance will need a SOW or order form that maps to our PO process. Do you template that?
[10:58] Maya: Yes, standard order form to capture committed tokens, billing cadence, billing entity, and SLAs. We'll include that in the package we send.
[11:05] Morgan: One open item — export controls. We flagged encryption export control language that may block some regions. How do you manage that?
[11:13] Tom: We follow export compliance; if a dataset or usage falls under controlled crypto/export restrictions we will highlight and propose mitigations. Usually this is handled in a DPA appendix.
[11:21] [pause, paper shuffling]
[11:30] Maya: OK let's recap quickly: Redwood to send MSA/DPA redlines + pricing worksheet + perf/runbook links. SE to attach Dedicated perf spreadsheet and canary guidance. Customer to confirm committed token volume and preferred billing entity, and legal to return DPA addendum items.
[11:45] Jill: We'll aim to have legal comments back within 7 business days.
[11:49] Rajesh: We'll scope the canary with Tom — looking for a small 2–3 node footprint in US-EAST to start.
[11:56] Maya: Great. Anybody else have burning questions?
[12:00] Samir: One last sec — will you allow our security team to onboard to the Console in read-only to validate audit logs?
[12:06] Maya: Yes, we can provision RBAC roles (read-only auditor) for your team. We'll include that in the onboarding checklist.
[12:12] Ivy: Thanks all.
[12:14] Maya: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the artifacts.
[12:18] [call ends]

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hearings: "K V" for KV cache, "redwood dedicated" lowercase or split in audio; some speaker labels merged (Morgan / Maya overlap) — verified by attendees in follow-ups. Links shared: (1) Redwood Dedicated perf spreadsheet — link to be sent, (2) Infosec pack (SOC2 + pen test) — folder link to be shared, (3) draft MSA/DPA redline — to be delivered with pricing worksheet.
